stations.design_purpose: The first station: assembled bare-handed from gathered wood and placed anywhere. Burns no fuel; it gates kit assembly, not metallurgy.
Placed from a Forge Kit assembled at the workbench. Its processes burn fuel (wood or charcoal), making power the fourth gate from the first hour.
Upgraded in place at a built forge. Consumes most of the mine-order payment plus useful output, so the upgrade feels earned through work rather than passively unlocked.

recipes.design_purpose: The start-with-nothing rung: gather wood by hand, lash a bench together in the field, place it (B, Tab to the kit).
Assembled at the workbench from all three gathered families, then placed to found the forge; replaces the pre-built forge site.
Slow-burned wood: four times the fuel value per unit, so smiths who plan their burns spend fewer trips hauling logs.
Two ore plus flux wood into one ingot; the forge also burns 2 fuel per smelt, so ore trips and wood trips stay coupled.

The first alloy (D-019): two ores that only surface once the deep wakes, combined at the forge you already have. Bronze is malleable and tough - the building family that works curved forms and the item base that holds a second modifier tier - so era two's new ground leads straight to era two's new work. Old ores never become trash: bronze needs copper forever.
The first weapon, craftable at the basic forge: its implicit physical damage is the first felt step above bare hands (D-014 slice 1).
The cold stat-stick needs the improved forge and Blacksmithing 3, so the freeze-shatter build is earned through the same forge ladder as armour.
The fire stat-stick sits on the same rung as the sceptre (improved forge, Blacksmithing 3) and burns one more charcoal: the two casting weapons are a choice, not a ladder.
Cheap third slot with a small resistance implicit; its rolled modifiers (from drops) are where a build gets pulled sideways.
The era-two weapon base: bronze from the deep, so a sceptre that can hold tier three is a sceptre with copper and tin trips behind it (D-019).
The era-two chest base that holds tier-three defence rolls.

catalyst_processes.status: provisional (Proposal C of ADR-0002; D-007 remains open)
catalyst_processes.design_purpose: The catalyst guarantees the domain (fire resistance lands, at tier 2) while the magnitude stays a bounded roll; minimum_roll_fraction raises the roll floor at the required skill so mastery buys consistency, and an existing better roll is never downgraded (preservation)

catalyst_processes.status: D-019: the preservation class of ADR-0002, doing its first real job
catalyst_processes.design_purpose: Moves the worn item's rolled modifiers, whole, onto a base in the pack of the same slot; the old base is spent with the catalyst. This is how a held-back roll is unleashed (an iron sceptre's tier-three cold onto bronze) and how a loved early find is never thrown away. The catalyst is the gate, not the skill: it drops rarely from the stone husks and shriekers of the hills and caves, and from elites' extra passes.

basic_temper.design_purpose: Quenching at a forge that supports basic_temper adds fire resistance at exactly the tier-1 midpoint, so the upgraded forge produces baseline resistance deterministically; the catalyst path is where the roll lives.

fuels.design_purpose: Fuel value per unit when a station process burns fuel. Charcoal concentrates wood four-to-one so refining fuel is worth forge time; the first rung of the power ladder (crafting-and-skills.md four gates).

craft_rolls.design_purpose: Crafted gear rolls modifiers like a drop (owner, 3 Sep 2026: 'they come out plain ... a random generation of modifiers is preferred'). A recipe whose output is an item base makes a rolled item in the pack instead of a stack: keen with keen_chance_at_level_1 plus keen_chance_per_level per Blacksmithing level above one, wrought (rolled first) from wrought_chance_from_level at wrought_chance_per_level per level above that, else plain. The tier is the era's, so era two's forge makes era two's rolls, and the seed is the craft count so a save replays its luck. Infrastructure stays the dependable route: the base is certain, the roll is the excitement.
